policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 13 Jan close (1x4 3.80, 3x6 3.55, 6x9 3.42, 9x12 3.39 vs WIBOR 3M 3.96) price roughly 55bp of NBP cuts within 12 months. The NBP survey of professional forecasters (2 Jan) sees an average reference rate of 3.69% in 2026. PKO (7 Jan): derivatives price a 3.25% reference rate by mid-2026; Deutsche Bank Polska (7 Jan) expects a January hold with core CPI at ~2.8%. MPC member Dąbrowski (Bloomberg, 8 Jan): a 50% chance of a January cut after the low December CPI, though he leans to a pause, and room for another 50bp by mid-2026; Tyrowicz (8 Jan): CPI may stay near target for the first time in this episode. PKO (12 Jan): only about half of a 25bp January cut is priced; Credit Agricole and Santander expect a hold, Goldman Sachs a cut. Parkiet poll (13 Jan): 3 of 19 teams expect a January cut, consensus two 25bp cuts in H1 2026; ING (13 Jan) puts a cut at 35% and sees a 3.25% terminal rate; MNI's survey shows most sell-side expecting a hold.
policy.risk_text: The January decision is a coin-toss for some members (Dąbrowski, 8 Jan) while most economists expect a hold: a hold would lift short FRAs/IRS a few bp (Millennium, 12-13 Jan), a cut would extend the front-end rally (PKO). If cuts are pushed beyond March, front-end roll-down does not materialise; heavy Q1 supply can widen asset swaps (Millennium, 9 Jan).

macro.projection_text: NBP November 2025 projection: CPI 3.7% (2025), 2.9% (2026), 2.5% (2027); December 2025 flash CPI 2.4% y/y.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit ~7.0% of GDP (MoF notified PLN 271bn; 4Q-rolling 7.0% after Q3 per Erste, 12 Jan); the Sejm completed the 2026 budget on 9 Jan (deficit cap PLN 271.7bn, gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn); presidential vetoes cost ~PLN 1.8bn in 2026 (Neneman, 9 Jan); budget cash PLN 133.8bn at end-Dec (MoF, 9 Jan). The President may send the budget to the Constitutional Tribunal (no veto right); the government would then run on its draft (Domański, 12 Jan).
macro.fiscal_risk_text: Q1 2026 supply of PLN 75-100bn over 8 auctions: PLN 13.7bn sold on 9 Jan, next 22 Jan (8-13bn) and 28 Jan (7-12bn); Fitch (27 Feb) and Moody's (20 Mar) reviews with negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut six times in 2025 to 4.00% (last on 3 Dec); CPI fell to 2.4% in December (flash, 31 Dec; final on 15 Jan, consensus 2.4% y/y, core ~2.8%), the NBP projects 2.9% for 2026 (professional forecasters, 2 Jan: 2.6%). Manufacturing PMI fell to 48.5 in December (2 Jan). GDP grew 3.8% y/y in Q3. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 13 Jan: US December core CPI 0.2% m/m (2.6% y/y vs 2.7% expected) left a Fed cut by June almost fully priced; Hungary CPI 3.3% (above the MNB projection), Czech CPI 2.1%; Brent rose ~2.5% on Iran. Poland's November current account showed a EUR 460m deficit (EUR 500m surplus expected); POLGB yields fell 3-4bp 'rather unexpectedly' (Erste). The 2026 budget reached the President on 13 Jan. Street views (December): PKO 1Q26 forecast 2Y 3.75 / 5Y 4.50 / 10Y 5.10 (reached by 7 Jan, PKO); Santander expects higher yields in Q1 on supply and cut repricing; ING says early-2026 trading follows MoF's Q1 issuance.

calendar.plan_text: MoF Q1 2026 financing plan (31 Dec 2025): 8 sale auctions for PLN 75-100bn, one switch auction, possible foreign issuance. January: sale auctions on 9 Jan (PLN 7-12bn), 22 Jan (8-13bn) and 28 Jan (7-12bn); no switch auction in January; 36-week T-bill auction on 16 Jan (PLN 2-4bn). 2026 gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn. BGK: FPC to issue domestically in 2026 (up to PLN 18.5bn). MoF priced EUR 3.25bn on 8 Jan (EUR 2bn Jan-2031 at 2.964%, MS+43; EUR 1.25bn Jun-2036 at 3.739%, MS+83). 9 Jan result: PLN 12.0bn sold vs 22.3bn demand (cover 1.86) plus 1.69bn additional sale (DS1035 1.17bn); stop yields OK0128 3.678%, PS0130 4.258%, PS0131 4.504%, DS1033 4.851%, DS1035 5.121%; new NZ0331 PLN 1.26bn at 95.20. Prefinancing at end-2025 was ~21% (final). MoF (12 Jan): 2026 needs ~26% financed. BGK sold PLN 3.73bn of FPC (demand 7.05bn) plus 0.71bn on 12 Jan. The 22 Jan offer had not been published by 13 Jan.
calendar.timing_text: Within each auction week of the Aug 2025-Jan 2026 sample, yields drifted lower into the auction (rally regime) and the auction-day close was the cheapest point relative to the preceding session, so new buying is best executed at the auction-day close (22, 28 Jan) rather than the day before. The 9 Jan auction cleared PLN 13.7bn with 1.86x cover, so supply is being absorbed; 22 and 28 Jan remain (PLN 15-25bn). For the front end the 13-14 Jan MPC is the event: a hold is the consensus, but Dąbrowski's 50% (8 Jan) means a cut is partly priced (about half, PKO 12 Jan); the December final CPI (15 Jan) and the March projection drive the timing.

Euro area.pricing: Hold at 2% priced through 2026 (7 Jan, after the flash HICP); Villeroy (12 Jan): a 2026 hike is 'fanciful'

United States.pricing: a cut by June almost fully priced after the soft core CPI (13 Jan); ~5% for January

Czechia.pricing: flat PRIBOR curve; CNB minutes (9 Jan): 6-0 hold, all options open

Hungary.pricing: BUBOR curve: mild easing priced; MNB (13 Jan): Dec CPI above projection, no January change

Later releases used where published by the info cut-off: Eurostat flash HICP 7 Jan, CZSO 7/13 Jan, KSH 13 Jan, BLS 13 Jan.
facts.core_text: Regime: the NBP paused at 4.00% with ~55bp more priced, the ECB is done at 2.00%, the Fed and BoE are easing gradually, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 59bp (Erste, 13 Jan close; its CDS/spread table looked stale). Soft US core CPI (13 Jan); Hungary's December CPI 3.3% came in above the MNB projection.

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).

12 Jan BGK auction: PLN 3.73bn sold against 7.05bn demand, plus 0.71bn in the additional sale (~PLN 4.4bn, about a quarter of the 2026 FPC plan of up to 18.5bn); per-series levels were not found. The 1.9x cover shows real-money demand for guaranteed paper at these spreads.
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
